title: Funnel congruency: why every step from ad to paywall must tell one story
summary: Jake Castillo argues that a frictionless app funnel depends on congruent messaging from top-of-funnel content through store page, onboarding and paywall. He borrows the native-ad funnel model, explains why one killer feature simplifies angles, and gives three benchmarks that diagnose which funnel step is broken.

principles.text: Make the funnel frictionless: customers should slide effortlessly down to the paywall, which requires every step to be congruent.
principles.quote: Your funnel needs to be as frictionless as possible.

principles.text: Carry the same language and pain point from top-of-funnel content through store page, onboarding and paywall.
principles.quote: Then every stage of the funnel afterwards (whether that’s your app store page or web2app funnel pages) need to carry the same messaging all the way through your onboarding to the paywall.

principles.text: Focus on one killer feature rather than several mediocre ones; it simplifies the marketing angles you use.
principles.quote: This is another reason why we only focused on one killer feature for Cal AI, and not 5 different mediocre ones, because this simplifies your marketing angles used to promote your product.

principles.text: Give prospects one idea to hold onto; each screen should confirm, not contradict, the story they're building.
principles.quote: Every screen after that either confirms or contradicts the story this prospect is constructing in their head about your solution.

principles.text: Native ad funnels work by educating first, so the product arrives as the answer to a problem, not a cold pitch.
principles.quote: And by then it doesn't feel like a pitch, it feels like the answer to a problem you are likely dealing with.

principles.text: Use benchmarks to locate the broken step: under 5 downloads/1,000 views, under 75% paywall rate, under 10% paywall conversion.
principles.quote: Under 5 downloads per 1,000 views? Your creative and your store page disagree.
